accepted.s: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at:
accepted.x: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at Marrakech in December 2018.
accepted.tq: Use the place–date pair to eliminate nearby international venues and years.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration:
1. It was endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly.
2. It is legally binding on all adopting countries.
3. It covers international migration, but not internal displacement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Compact was endorsed by the UN General Assembly and covers international migration only. It is non-binding, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the false legal-status statement and distinguish international migration from internal displacement.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following countries stayed out of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration?
accepted.x: The United States stayed out of the Global Compact; therefore, not all UN members adopted it.
accepted.tq: Apply the membership-exception trap to a multilateral compact.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the geographical pattern of international migrants?
o: Europe has the highest migrant share, UAE has the largest number of migrants, and Asia has the highest percentage
UAE has the highest migrant share, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and Oceania has the highest percentage of migrants
Oceania has the highest migrant share, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and UAE has the highest percentage
Qatar has the highest migrant share, Oceania has the largest number of migrants, and Europe has the highest percentage
accepted.x: The UAE has the highest migrant share of population, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and Oceania has the highest percentage of migrants.
accepted.tq: Keep absolute number, population share and regional percentage as separate comparisons.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s: According to the World Migration Report 2026, the number of international migrants and their share in world population are approximately:
accepted.x: The World Migration Report 2026 gives 304 million international migrants, constituting 3.7 per cent of the world population. The earlier 2 per cent figure is outdated.
accepted.tq: Match the current population figure with its corresponding percentage rather than the outdated estimate.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s:
The World Migration Report 2026 is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Thirteenth edition
2. Published by the International Organization for Migration
3. Published every two years since 2000
4. IOM founded in 1951
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the 2026 report is the thirteenth edition, is published by IOM, follows a biennial series since 2000, and IOM was founded in 1951.
accepted.tq: Check each independent edition, institution, periodicity and founding-year detail.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the displacement figures reported in the World Migration Report 2026?
o: 905 million forcibly displaced and 304 million disaster-induced internal displacements
65.8 million forcibly displaced and more than 120 million disaster-induced internal displacements
More than 120 million international migrants and 65.8 million total migrants
More than 120 million forcibly displaced and 65.8 million internal displacements caused by disasters
accepted.x: The report records more than 120 million forcibly displaced people and 65.8 million internal displacements caused by disasters.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing two closely related displacement figures and their causes.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s: Global remittances amounted to approximately what figure in 2024, according to the World Migration Report 2026?
accepted.x: Global remittances were reported at approximately USD 905 billion in 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the global remittance total from India’s remittance receipt and migrant totals.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India and international migration:
1. India has the largest diaspora in the world.
2. India is the only country receiving remittances above USD 100 billion.
3. India received USD 137 billion in remittances in 2024.
4. India-UAE is the fifth-largest migration corridor and India-US is the sixth-largest.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct according to the World Migration Report 2026 figures for India’s diaspora, remittances and migration corridors.
accepted.tq: Combine several country-specific facts while checking rankings and the precise remittance figure.
accepted.sec: International migration - Global Compact for Migration, regions and countries with highest migrant share  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following countries are specifically identified as Gulf states having a high share of migrants in their populations?
1. United Arab Emirates
2. Qatar
3. Kuwait
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The UAE, Qatar and Kuwait are all identified as Gulf states with a high share of migrants in their populations.

accepted.x: India signed a Migration and Mobility Partnership with Moldova during 2024–25.

accepted.s: The Pre-Departure Orientation Training programme of the Ministry of External Affairs had trained how many emigrant workers by December 2024?
accepted.x: The MEA’s PDOT, initiated in January 2018, had trained 1,72,220 emigrant workers by December 2024.
accepted.tq: Link the exact programme figure with its time boundary and avoid nearby rounded values.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an internal migration?
o: Movement of a refugee across an international border
Movement of an illegal immigrant into another country
Movement from one Indian state to another
Movement from India to the United Arab Emirates
accepted.x: Internal migration takes place within a country, including movement between states, districts, towns and villages. The other examples involve international migration.
accepted.tq: Apply the administrative-boundary test to distinguish internal and international migration.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets correctly classifies migration on the basis of administrative boundary?
accepted.x: Administrative boundary produces the classification of internal and international migration. The other pairs are based on time, number and will respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each classification pair with its correct basis.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: Harvest labour migration is generally an example of:
accepted.x: Migration associated with harvest labour is generally temporary or seasonal because it is linked to a recurring period of agricultural work.
accepted.tq: Use the duration of stay and the agricultural context to identify the migration type.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Basis)
a. Distance
b. Number
c. Cause
d. Will

List-II (Classification)
i. Individual or mass
ii. Economic, social, political or religious
iii. Voluntary or forced
iv. Short-distance or long-distance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Distance corresponds to short- or long-distance migration; number to individual or mass; cause to economic, social, political or religious; and will to voluntary or forced.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and match each classification with its stated basis.

accepted.s: A person who leaves a place because of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or membership of a social or political group, and cannot return safely, is called a:
accepted.x: A refugee is forced to leave and cannot return because of fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality or social or political group.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise legal-social definition from its cause and inability to return.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a form of forced migration identified in the classification of migration by will?
accepted.x: Weighing push and pull factors is associated with voluntary migration. Persecution, development-induced displacement and exploitation are causes of forced migration.
accepted.tq: Find the one item belonging to voluntary rather than forced migration.

accepted.s: Return migration refers to:
o: Permanent movement across an international boundary
Going back to the original place once the cause of migration is over
Movement from a village to a town for the first time
accepted.x: Return migration means going back to the previous place after the cause that led to migration has ended.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence of departure, end of cause and return to identify the concept.

accepted.s: Under the Census method based on place of birth, migrants are identified as:
accepted.x: The place-of-birth method gives lifetime migrants. The Census also uses place of last residence as another method.
accepted.tq: Separate the Census place-of-birth method from the place-of-last-residence method.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Census uses place of birth to identify lifetime migrants.
2. The Census also uses place of last residence.
3. PLFS and NSO use a Usual Place of Residence criterion involving at least six months of residence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Census uses both place of birth and place of last residence, while PLFS and NSO apply the Usual Place of Residence criterion of at least six months.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two Census methods from the usual-residence rule used by PLFS and NSO.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: A person whose current place differs from the place of last residence is treated as a migrant under the Census definition. Under the alternative method, the relevant reference point is the:
accepted.x: The Census identifies migration using place of last residence or, under the other method, place of birth.
accepted.tq: Test the paired reference points used in the two Census migration methods.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: The Usual Place of Residence criterion used by PLFS and NSO generally requires a person to have lived at a place for at least:
accepted.x: PLFS and NSO use the Usual Place of Residence criterion, with residence for at least six months.
accepted.tq: Recall the duration threshold and distinguish it from the short-term migration definition.

accepted.s: The Nationwide Migration Survey conducted by MoSPI for July 2026–June 2027 is significant because it is:
o: The first international migration survey since 1951
The first full migration survey since 2007–08
The first survey limited to seasonal agricultural labour
The first Census survey based only on place of birth

accepted.s: Under the revised definition proposed for the MoSPI Nationwide Migration Survey, short-term migration refers to migration lasting:
accepted.x: The revised definition treats short-term migration as lasting from 15 days to 6 months; earlier, the period was 1 to 6 months.
accepted.tq: Compare the revised lower limit with the earlier one-month lower limit.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the earlier and revised definitions of short-term migration in the MoSPI survey?
o: Earlier: less than 15 days; revised: more than 6 months
accepted.x: The earlier definition covered 1–6 months, whereas the revised definition covers 15 days–6 months.
accepted.tq: Use the changed boundary value to discriminate between two otherwise similar definitions.
accepted.sec: Migration types - internal vs international, permanent vs seasonal, forced vs voluntary

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Internal migration — between villages, towns, districts or states
Permanent migration — classification by administrative boundary
International migration — legal immigrants, illegal immigrants and refugees
accepted.x: Permanent migration is a classification by time, not by administrative boundary. Administrative boundary distinguishes internal and international migration.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched basis rather than judging the migration term in isolation.
